item.title: Galois's lost proof on $PSL(2,p)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In his famous ``testamentary letter'' Galois formulated several results without proof. Among them he claimed --- here we express it in modern terms --- that the projective special linear group $PSL(2,p)$ has a subgroup of index $p$ only for $p\le 11$. Nowadays this result is seen as a corollary of the complete enumeration of all subgroups of $PSL(2,p)$ obtained by Gierster in 1881. In this paper we attempt to give a proof that uses only methods available to Galois.
item.dc:creator: P\'eter P. P\'alfy

item.title: A Rightly Forgotten Mathematician? Jozsef Sutak (1865--1954) and Budapest Mathematics between Bolyai and the Numerus Clausus
item.description: arXiv:2603.22196v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: J\'ozsef Sut\'ak (1865--1954), a Piarist priest, \emph{gymnasium} teacher and from 1912 full professor of geometry at the University of Budapest, is scarcely more than a footnote in the history of Hungarian mathematics. His name survives mainly because he co-signed, with Lip\'ot Fej\'er, the acceptance of John von Neumann's 1926 dissertation on the axiomatic construction of set theory. Drawing on his printed works, on the records of the Budapest Faculty of Philosophy and of the Catholic Saint Stephen Academy, and on a hitherto unknown part of his personal papers, this article reconstructs his career. It follows his Hungarian translation of Bolyai's \emph{Appendix} (1897), his empiricist lecture on the axioms of geometry (1898), his papers on the logical problems of set theory (1911) and on the axiomatic construction of projective geometry (1914), and his later differential-geometric work. It analyses his appointment in 1911/12, when the faculty preferred him to Frigyes Riesz and Alfr\'ed Haar, and his role as chairman of the admissions committee in implementing the numerus clausus after 1920. The answer to the title's question is twofold: as a mathematician, Sut\'ak is largely rightly forgotten; for the history of Budapest mathematics and its university, he is not.
item.dc:creator: Andras Batkai

item.title: On the role of Giovanni Giorgi in the history of operational methods for mathematical-physics problems
item.description: arXiv:2608.15575v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we discuss the historical role played by Prof. Giovanni Giorgi (1871-1950) in the development of operational methods in mathematical physics. In the literature, the analysis of the scientific contributions of Giorgi is discussed in many historical papers mainly about the $MKS\Omega$-system and its contributions in the field of electrical engineering. Starting from the obituary written by Prof. Dario Graffi (1905-1990), here we analyze in detail the contributions given by Giorgi in mathematical physics, especially in the framework of the studies started by Heaviside (1850-1925) in order to obtain a symbolic representation of the solutions of differential equations emerging in physical problems. \\ Moreover, we underline the little known contribution of Giorgi to the analysis of derivatives of any real order, namely fractional derivatives, according to the present notation. \\ The main aim of this note is to underline the historical relevance of Giorgi in the mathematical foundations of operational methods in relation to the solutions of concrete problems emerging in applied physics.
item.dc:creator: R. Garra, F. Mainardi
